outlines.title: Choose a maintenance scope across competing firmware branches
outlines.objective: Authorize a technically credible maintenance commitment balancing security exposure, operational importance and branch-specific engineering effort.
outlines.decision_problem: The backlog contains security corrections and functional defects that share some code but differ in hardware compatibility and customer consequences. A proposed common backport overstates reusable work; source differences and qualification history may require separate changes on older branches. The developer establishes reusable versus branch-specific work and substantiates effort. The security analyst assesses exposure under deferral, while the application engineer evaluates critical functions and mitigation costs. The manager creates the plan, reconciles protected support capacity and chooses among materially different feasible scopes using fixed workspace rules. The comparison preserves dependencies, uncertainty and deferred obligations. Authorized work, acceptance conditions and reassessment commitments flow into engineering issues, the maintenance decision and support-facing availability statements. Selecting work establishes a planning commitment, not qualification or release readiness.

assumptions: Clearwater Protection Systems is fictional. Its unit structure, scale, customer population, products, branch names, workload, archive and authority limits are synthetic, not SEL counts or reporting-line claims.

The six workers represent recurring participants within a 24-person unit. Other employees' ordinary support and development commitments appear in existing records; those employees need not act to finish an episode.
All worker SOC codes come from the supplied occupation list. Roles follow the sustaining-firmware operation rather than manufacturing occupation quotas.

All participants use computer-use automation (CUA) and bash in separate personal virtual machines (VMs), accessing shared applications. The entire unit workspace may be shared; artificial secrecy is unnecessary.

The declared runtime uses shared_session identity. In-app usernames, assignees, reviewers and document owners cannot independently prove worker authorship or technical approval. Attribute contributions through worker VM records and explicit worker identifiers.

Every required app has a separate origin. Seed every documented top-level state key and no undocumented keys. Access differences use VM-level app URLs, not assumed server-enforced per-worker permissions.

The six selected applications are within available_runtime_apps. No deployed surface manifest or independent runtime validation was supplied. Mounts, source readability, shared persistence, interface behavior and reset behavior remain explicit construction gaps.

The supplied https://selinc.com/products/710-5/ capture is unreadable with error 'ValueError: empty page or access challenge'. Its purported quotation is removed and the page supplies no operational evidence. The replacement hardware-applicability claim uses the successfully read SEL-710 Card Options PDF, date code 20190508.

The dated hardware-applicability evidence establishes a particular dependency, not present-day compatibility across SEL products. Episode-specific compatibility, rollback and qualification facts must be supplied in underlying synthetic technical records.

Populate readable source snapshots, configuration histories, manifests, completed test reports and customer correspondence before execution. A filename, upload status, green check, shipment record or merged pull request alone cannot establish tested behavior, installed firmware or release readiness.

GitHub holds engineering records, Drive holds supporting evidence, Docs holds analysis and guidance, Gmail holds correspondence, Slack holds coordination and Calendar holds commitments. Stable case, device, build, branch and report identifiers connect records; synchronization is not assumed.

Seeded regression policy contains general evidence-applicability, operational-function and customer-guidance requirements. It must not contain resolved customer-specific recovery choices, promise restrictions or causal explanations. Preserve underlying reports, compatibility facts and customer preferences; keep resolved conclusions in private evaluation.
Historical upload failures may inform provenance only if their records are inspectable. Completion must not require retrying uploads or treating upload metadata as qualification evidence.

Each episode fixes capacity, priorities, risk categories, compatibility requirements and disclosure authority in its starting workspace. Dates express internal commitments; fictional vulnerabilities and firmware versions do not depend on changing live web state.
Managers receive objectives and create their own plans. Outline contributions identify necessary expertise and downstream dependencies without prescribing a delegation sequence.

All outlines finish through analysis, review and internal record updates. Laboratory work, firmware signing, distribution, external replies, customer outages and field installation remain downstream boundaries; no clock acceleration is required.

Customer-facing outputs remain internally approved, unsent drafts unless a later assignment explicitly authorizes transmission. Holds, returns and deferred maintenance preserve specific unresolved obligations.
